The item delivered to me is not the same as what is shown on the Amazon site.

See my photos. The original OEM Kenmore filter is at the top of each photo; replacement air filter from Amazon on bottom.

While the replacement filter does fit properly in my Kenmore refrigerator, the materials and construction are decidedly different than the OEM filter that came with the refrigerator. The original OEM Kenmore filter is constructed with the black, perforated (punched holes) carbon filter sandwiched between two sheets of white fabric filter material. The air filter replacement delivered from Amazon (from LG?) is made of a black "honeycomb" material (tiny holes) and lacked the two sheets of fabric filter material. However, the replacement does appear to have a black fabric material laminated to one side of the carbon filter.

Is the replacement a fair replacement or improved design? We'll see. I'm not a fan of inaccurate/false advertising, so 2 stars until the item supplied matches what they are advertising.

I purchased the Simple cup reusable K-cups last year for my then-new K-50 coffee maker.

I now use them with some caution. I still like the system.

Don't overfill,or overpack (i.e. tamp) these cups. The Keurig is not an espresso maker.

When you fill them, use a teaspoon or small spoon to loosely load the coffee in the container and filter, before pushing the cap on the unit. If there are some extra dry grounds on the cap afterwards, either shake the excess coffee back in your coffee supply, or discard the remainder. You don't want the extra grounds on the cap surface.

I learned my lesson after having coffee grounds clog the machine. I was tired, got sloppy and stuffed the cup and filter with too much coffee. Then, I couldn't get the Keurig to brew properly. My award for my impatience was the receipt of a weak cup of lukewarm amber water with some coffee grounds in it. It looked more like the tap water in my old apartment.

Fortunately, and with some patience, I was able remedy the problem by using a paper clip to unclog the three nozzle assembly, and flush the reservoir to resolve the problem. My next step was to use vinegar on the initial flush, and enough water to flush the vinegar smell out of the unit afterwards. If you use these filters exclusively, consider brewing a cup of hot water weekly (no K-Kup or Simple Cup inserted in machine) through the system to prevent clog problems.

This is an interesting side-step to loading your own pods, which creates additional problems instead of solving them. The paper filters do NOT fit completely into the plastic holder, resulting in the possibility of a broken filter after brewing (messy cleanup) but certainly not permitting as much ground coffee in the pod, making for a weaker brew.
A side-step is to carefully push the filter fully into the pod, which takes some practice as it wants to retain its' formed shape.
The top is another questionable exercise in patience, as filling the pod with grounds level to the edge makes it too full to cover with the top, leading to a coffee spill or grounds coming out of the top.
All in all I will not recommend this product.
